item.title: 700 supermarkets hit, millions lost: France warns refrigeration cyberattacks may persist
item.description: A cyberattack targeting refrigeration systems at supermarkets in France has led to significant disruptions in food supply chains. The attack, which occurred on Monday, affected approximately 700 supermarkets, causing spoilage and financial losses. Authorities warn that the cyber threats might still be active, urging retailers to enhance their security measures. Investigations are ongoing, but no group has claimed responsibility for these incidents.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 3 Indians killed in Germany fire, 5 injured; resident arrested on murder suspicion
item.description: The victims were two women aged 25 and 27, and a 26-year-old man, German public broadcaster WDR reported, citing Bochum police. Their identities and home states in India have not been disclosed. The five injured people suffered smoke inhalation and were taken to hospitals in Bochum. Their nationalities have not been reported.

item.title: New Yorker’s $3 yard sale bowl sells for $2.2 million
item.description: A remarkable discovery unfolded in 2007 when a New Yorker purchased a small white bowl for merely three dollars during a yard sale. For years, this bowl was displayed proudly in their home until appraisers revealed its true worth: a rare 'Ding' ware from the Northern Song dynasty valued between $200,000 to $300,000. The piece garnered attention and sold for an astounding $2,225,000 at a Sotheby’s auction in March 2013.

item.title: Selena Gomez’s Rare Impact Fund raises $30 million to support youth mental health worldwide
item.description: Selena Gomez's Rare Impact Fund is dedicated to advancing youth mental health resources and education across the globe. Having already generated over $30 million, the fund collaborates with 30 nonprofits on five continents. Its goal is to raise $100 million to broaden mental health care accessibility. Recent events have gained traction, drawing support from various corporations and celebrities, highlighting the need for ongoing community engagement to meet these ambitious targets.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pierre Cardin restored the Marquis de Sade’s ruined French château, turning it into a festival venue
item.description: Since its acquisition by Pierre Cardin in 2001, Château de Lacoste has seen remarkable renovations. This historic castle, once associated with the Marquis de Sade, is now a vibrant performing arts hub, hosting the annual Festival de Lacoste. This festival showcases opera, dance, and classical theatre in an enchanting open-air amphitheatre.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Demolition Rule Changes Pause: Saratoga Springs mayor halts plan after opposition; safeguards stay
item.description: Saratoga Springs Mayor John Safford has paused changes to historic building demolition rules following community backlash. Opposition arose during a public hearing where residents and preservationists expressed their concerns. The current demolition safeguards will remain while the city reviews its development regulations. Safford intends to revise other parts of the development rules despite the current pause. A City Council public hearing is scheduled, allowing further community input on proposed amendments.

item.title: In 1991, Steve Harvey slept in his car with $35. After Apollo fame, his foundation awarded $700,000
item.description: Steve Harvey faced significant financial struggles in the early 1990s, paving the way for his journey to becoming a prominent entertainer and philanthropist. He founded the Steve & Marjorie Harvey Foundation, which has invested over $700,000 in college scholarships, catering to youth from low-income families. Additionally, the foundation emphasizes mentorship programs aiming to cultivate leadership skills among the young, creating numerous opportunities for underprivileged communities throughout North America.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tyler Perry transformed Atlanta’s 330-acre army base into a film hub with 12 sound stages
item.description: In 2015, Tyler Perry acquired the former Fort McPherson Army base in Atlanta for $30 million, and transformed it into a major production hub featuring 12 sound stages. This initiative not only aims to create new jobs but also emphasizes the importance of preserving historical structures while meeting the evolving demands of the film industry. Perry’s vision includes nurturing local talent to foster growth in South Atlanta's creative landscape.

item.title: Michael Jordan’s 1998 Bulls jersey sells for record $14 million to Miami investor
item.description: A historic Michael Jordan jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals has been sold for an astonishing $14 million. This sale sets a new benchmark in the world of basketball collectibles, emphasizing the increasing importance of sports memorabilia in popular culture. With its autograph and verified ownership, the jersey's value soared, especially as interest in Jordan's last championship season continues to grow, attracting avid collectors and investors alike.

item.title: New York art teacher’s thrift-store painting bought for under $100 sells for £189,200 after 60 years
item.description: A remarkable transformation has occurred for a painting acquired for under $100, which has now fetched an astonishing £189,200 due to its true provenance being uncovered. Hidden for decades within a family's home, the artwork, initially misattributed, is revealed to be the work of Scottish artist Francis Campbell Boileau Cadell.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Very risky choice’: Meloni warns US-Russia diesel deal could help fund Ukraine war
item.description: Giorgia Meloni has expressed concerns about the US agreement with Russia regarding diesel supplies during her parliament address. She believes the deal could financially aid Russia's war efforts in Ukraine. Meloni urged the European Union to appoint a representative for negotiating peace talks with Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized the agreement, stating it could further support Moscow's military actions.
